method: judging.md section 10: claims from the arm's own notes checked against its canonical renders in render/ and facts.json; the checker does not score or compare arms

claims.claim: Headline uses the brief's message nearly verbatim ("Your app's data lives on the device first."); the lede adds what it is (open-source, local-first SQL database) so the first screen answers "what is it" and "how do I start" (npm install + Get started).
claims.evidence: desktop-01.png and mobile-01.png: H1 'Your app's data lives on the device first.', lede opens 'Driftless is an open-source, local-first SQL database', npm install box with Copy and a Get started button all in the first screen at both sizes.

claims.claim: Code sample: same statements, identifiers and SQL as the brief, but line breaks rewrapped (max ~41 chars per line) so it stays legible at 390 px with no horizontal scroll and no clipping.
claims.evidence: desktop-01.png shows all 19 lines with the brief's statements and identifiers; mobile-01.png/mobile-02.png show the same 19 lines with no line wrapped or cut at 390; facts.json horizontal_overflow false at 390x844@2. The rewrap applies on desktop too.

claims.claim: Swift and Gradle install lines live in the "Get started" block near the end; the hero shows only the npm command with a pointer to the others.
claims.evidence: desktop-01.png hero: npm only plus 'Swift and Gradle packages below'; desktop-06.png/desktop-07.png and mobile-10.png: Get started block lists npm, Swift Package Manager and Gradle lines.

claims.claim: Step 2 and step 3 illustrations (a "title"/"done" row merged per column; a shape WHERE team_id = ? relaying to two of three devices); the 0.8 ms figure is shown under step 1.
claims.evidence: desktop-02.png and mobile-03.png/mobile-04.png: step 1 shows 'local write · p50 0.8 ms'; step 2 table Laptop/Phone/Merged over title and done columns; step 3 'shape: WHERE team_id = ?' with Browser team 7 and Android team 7 ticked and Desktop team 9 dashed.

claims.claim: "Works offline" card says changes "sync when the network returns"; "690 KB in the browser" card says storage is OPFS and data persists between sessions.
claims.evidence: desktop-04.png and mobile-06.png: both cards carry that wording.

claims.claim: Pricing: Cloud Pro is visually outlined because it is the paid self-serve plan; no "most popular" or similar claim is made.
claims.evidence: desktop-05.png and mobile-07.png/mobile-08.png: Pro card has a heavy dark outline and the only filled CTA ('Start with Pro'); no badge or 'popular/recommended' text anywhere in the frames.

claims.claim: Plan rows are ordered so synced data / devices / support line up between Hobby and Pro.
claims.evidence: desktop-05.png: row 1 '1 GB' / '25 GB synced data', row 2 '500' / '25,000 monthly active devices', row 4 'Community support' / 'Email support'.

claims.claim: On mobile the plans are titled "Cloud Hobby / Cloud Pro / Cloud Enterprise" instead of a separate "Driftless Cloud" label.
claims.evidence: mobile-07.png/mobile-08.png: titles 'Cloud Hobby', 'Cloud Pro', 'Cloud Enterprise' with no eyebrow; desktop-05.png keeps the 'DRIFTLESS CLOUD' eyebrow.

claims.claim: Nav on mobile collapses to logo + Get started + a menu button (simple JS toggle); all page content is visible without interaction.
claims.evidence: mobile-01.png: header shows logo, Get started and a hamburger button; the header stays on every mobile frame (mobile-02..10.png), and every section renders open in the static frames. The toggle itself is behaviour a static render cannot show.

claims.claim: Mobile page was kept under ~8,100 CSS px so the full-page 2x capture fits in the 10 reviewed screens.
claims.evidence: facts/render.json: mobile page height 8055 px, 10 frames, truncated false; mobile-10.png ends at the footer.

claims.claim: Social proof used is only the listed 18.4k stars, 236 contributors and 1.2M npm downloads/month (Aug 2026).
claims.evidence: desktop-01.png and mobile-02.png: exactly those three figures, plus the GitHub 18.4k count in the desktop nav; no logos, quotes or testimonials in any frame.

claims.claim: All graphics (logo mark, contour-line background, icons, diagrams) are hand-made inline SVG/HTML; fonts are Geist and Geist Mono.
claims.evidence: The logo mark, contour-line background (desktop-01.png, mobile-01.png), icons and diagrams are on screen, but how they were made and which font files loaded are process and provenance, not visible in a render.

notes: The arm makes no contrast claim, so nothing is contradicted there; for the record, facts.json has 2 text nodes below AA at both sizes (4.24:1, 12.5px #b8561b on #f4f1ea, the orange 'Q3 roadmap' and '1' cells in the step 2 merge table, desktop-02.png, mobile-03.png). Link targets being placeholders, the Playwright render process and the Octicon licence are not visual claims and were not counted.
